question: Can a physically meaningful Poisson/count-variance data fidelity be derived from session B, and would it improve held-out B prediction and the flat-profile bias over the existing correlation+MSE+CV objective?
decision_reason: A defensible Poisson likelihood cannot be derived from the stored data. Blocking preconditions fail (see blocking_reasons). Per the task rule, the script stops and explains why instead of inventing a noise model.

blocking_reasons.name: independently_measured_offset
blocking_reasons.explanation: No dark/offset frame exists in the session. The only additive offset is the radiometry bias_counts from the session-A fit, which the codebase documents as not independently identifiable without a dark/response experiment. A Poisson mean cannot be separated into light + measured offset from these data.

blocking_reasons.name: camera_conversion_gain

evidence.source_note: Reads light_check.json metadata only; no image rows, no split dependence.
evidence.note: counts_per_ms is an optical count-rate, not the camera ADU/e- conversion gain; no e-/ADU value is stored.

blocking_reasons.explanation: Poisson statistics apply to photoelectrons. Without the ADU/e- conversion gain the variance of an ADU count is unknown up to a multiplicative factor, so an absolute Poisson likelihood cannot be formed.

blocking_reasons.name: poisson_variance_law

evidence.note: Computed from B train rows only; no test row contributes to this decision.

blocking_reasons.explanation: Per-pixel temporal variance is about 0.3x the mean, not ~1x. The recorded ADU are strongly sub-Poisson (consistent with ~3 e-/ADU or on-camera averaging), so a var=mean likelihood mis-weights pixels by roughly 3x and mis-models the near-deterministic pedestal.

checks.name: integer_raw_counts
checks.explanation: raw_frames are integer ADU with repeated frames, so a count law is at least representable.

checks.name: per_row_exposure_ms
checks.explanation: Every train/test row carries a positive exposure in ms.

checks.name: signal_linear_in_exposure
checks.explanation: Core counts scale with exposure like light; the additive background does not scale with exposure, so it is a constant pedestal rather than ambient (Poisson) light.

checks.name: independently_measured_offset
checks.explanation: No dark/offset frame exists in the session. evidence.note: counts_per_ms is an optical count-rate, not the camera ADU/e- conversion gain; no e-/ADU value is stored.

checks.explanation: Poisson statistics apply to photoelectrons. Without the ADU/e- conversion gain the variance of an ADU count is unknown up to a multiplicative factor, so an absolute Poisson likelihood cannot be formed.

checks.explanation: Per-pixel temporal variance is about 0.3x the mean, not ~1x. The recorded ADU are strongly sub-Poisson (consistent with ~3 e-/ADU or on-camera averaging), so a var=mean likelihood mis-weights pixels by roughly 3x and mis-models the near-deterministic pedestal.

checks.name: background_quantisation
checks.explanation: Nearly all background pixels are exactly 0 or 1 ADU and the mean is below one ADU, so the background is quantisation-limited, not a sampled Poisson light level.

checks.name: stored_target_is_count_rate

evidence.source_note: Describes how fit.load_dataset stores the target; no image rows involved.

checks.explanation: The fit compares count-rate images, not integer total counts. A Poisson likelihood would need N=sum(raw_frames) and a mean that also carries the three-frame stack, which the current target does not.

decision_data_policy.rule: Every decision-driving / blocking check is free of test-row influence. Row-derived checks (integer_raw_counts, per_row_exposure_ms, signal_linear_in_exposure, independently_measured_offset, poisson_variance_law, background_quantisation) are computed from B train rows only (source_split=train). camera_conversion_gain reads dataset metadata only (source_split=dataset_metadata), and stored_target_is_count_rate is a code-definition fact (source_split=code_definition); neither uses any image row, so neither can depend on the test split.
decision_data_policy.test_rows: Held-out B test rows appear only in data_inventory.exposure_groups_test as descriptive aggregates. They never determine decision, blockers, thresholds, or the fit plan, and no parameter is fit or selected on them.

data_inventory.exposure_groups_note: exposure_groups is an all-split descriptive aggregate and is NOT used by any decision; decision checks use exposure_groups_train only.

units_and_offsets.raw_frames: integer ADU, repeated frames; summed for a count target

intended_design.start: session-A fit_m3_full frozen parameters (defocus, amplitude centre/width, residual Z5..Z11) with B's ramp matrix re-fitted from B's signed ramp pairs and origin re-anchored to B's reference_start; adaptation=full.
comparison: baseline: existing correlation + 0.25*relative_mse + 0.25*CV, fitted on B train only
treatment: Poisson NLL on integer total counts versus the same full physical forward fitted on B train only
intended_design.same_start_same_budget: identical initial parameters and identical number of optimizer steps for both objectives; model frozen before test
intended_design.freeze_then_test: select on train, freeze, then report signed Pearson, relative L2, CV absolute error and the flat-profile bias on the 24 test rows; no test tuning
intended_design.not_run_reason: A defensible Poisson likelihood cannot be derived from the stored data. Blocking preconditions fail (see blocking_reasons). Per the task rule, the script stops and explains why instead of inventing a noise model.

what_would_make_it_defensible: Capture a blocked-beam dark frame stack at each exposure (0.028 and 0.051 ms) to measure the per-pixel bias and its temporal noise.
Capture an exposure-response series to estimate the ADU/e- conversion gain and read noise from variance versus mean; verify var/mean ~ 1/gain.
Re-run this diagnostic; if var/mean ~ 1/gain and a measured dark exists, use a Poisson (or Poisson+read-noise / Pearson chi-square) likelihood on dark-subtracted integer counts.

authoritative_context.known_bias_to_test: flat/smooth-profile contrast: predicted CV is biased relative to measured (cv_prediction rose +0.45 in the session-A comparison); this is the target of the Poisson experiment.
